name: Mike Patrick
role: U.S. Army — believed a ranger with a MACV special operations group
summary: The tall American at the center of the strike-force group photo on Núi Bà Đen (VN-0010), arm around one of the trainees. Larry thinks he was a ranger with a special operations group for MACV, and says he was what you would call a ghost or a spook — though Larry doesn't know why he was called that.
researchNotes: One of the few people in the archive with both a first and last name — genuinely searchable. 'Special operations group for MACV' reads naturally as MACV-SOG (activated January 1964), which would fit the 'ghost'/'spook' reputation and the duck-hunter-camouflaged irregulars around him; treat as a lead against SOG rosters and association membership lists, not a settled assignment. He is a strong candidate to have known the Núi Bà Đen camp personnel (Lowry, unresolved #4). 2026-08-23 (giscus-vn-0010-c18119905): Larry named the organisation himself — "He was above special forces. He was MAGSOG." His own rendering of MACV-SOG, which the survey had only inferred from "special operations group for MACV." Still his single testimony rather than a document, so the classification does not move; but the reading is now his, not the archive's.
